rules.title: Kumbhalgarh sanctuary: entry permit from forest office
rules.detail: A 2017 guide says the forest office at Sadri issues the entry permit, with a charge per visitor and per two-wheeler. No government order was found.

rules.title: Kumbhalgarh sanctuary: shut 1 July to 30 September
rules.detail: Safaris in the sanctuary stop every year for the monsoon and resume on 1 October. Visits inside are by hired jeep from the gates. The order itself was not read.

source.title: Jeep Safari Resumes At Jaisamand-Kumbhalgarh Sanctuary After 3-Month Break

history.change: Jeep safaris resumed at Kumbhalgarh, Jaisamand and Bassi sanctuaries after the yearly monsoon closure.

source.title: Jeep Safari Resumes At Jaisamand-Kumbhalgarh Sanctuary After 3-Month Break

season.note: The cool dry months suit this route; Mount Abu gets very heavy rain in July and August, and the Kumbhalgarh sanctuary is shut from July to September.

history.note: Yearly monsoon closure of safaris inside the Kumbhalgarh sanctuary, not of public roads. Safaris resumed on 1 October 2024.

hazards.title: Very heavy monsoon rain on Mount Abu
hazards.detail: July and August each bring more than 500 millimetres of rain to the hill, on a climb of steady bends from Abu Road.

hazards.title: Cold winter mornings on Mount Abu
hazards.detail: Average winter minimums fall to between 3 and 12 degrees Celsius at 4,000 feet.

gaps: Mount Abu entry toll for vehicles: two searches found no official or news page stating who collects it or whether two-wheelers pay.
Kumbhalgarh sanctuary fees and gate hours: only non-official pages give amounts, and they disagree, so amounts are left out. The Rajasthan Forest Department portal showed no readable content.

Whether a private motorcycle may enter the Kumbhalgarh sanctuary is unclear: a 2017 guide lists a two-wheeler charge, while a 2025 guide (https://roundglasssustain.com/habitats/guide-kumbhalgarh-and-todgarh-raoli) mentions only hired jeeps.
No source found for gate timings or two-wheeler rules inside the Mount Abu Wildlife Sanctuary. Its eco-sensitive zone was notified on 2020-11-11 per Wikipedia, with no rider rule stated.
The highway numbers for Udaipur to Kumbhalgarh and Kumbhalgarh to Ranakpur were not sourced.
Usual number of riding days: no source found.
The Rajasthan tourism site loads its text by script and could not be read.
Videos: the pages give upload dates, not filming dates, so 'filmed' is filled only where the title names a date. Uploads, in order: 2024-03, 2025-07.
